```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Chen_2026_danicopan"))
```

* Citation: `r mod$reference`
* Description: `r mod$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70209>
* Open-access full text: <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12947316/>

Danicopan is an oral complement factor D inhibitor approved as add-on therapy
to the C5 inhibitors ravulizumab or eculizumab for clinically significant
extravascular hemolysis in paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH). Chen
2026 pools 14 studies into a population PK model and links it to a direct
inhibitory Emax model of serum complement alternative pathway (AP) activity,
measured by hemolysis assay in the phase 3 ALPHA study. Both layers are in the
one model file: the PK model predicts `Cc` (ng/mL) and the PK-PD model turns
`Cc` into `alternative_pathway_activity` (% of reference serum activity).

# Population

The PK dataset holds 7491 post-dose plasma concentrations from 407
participants: 316 healthy participants from 11 phase 1 studies and 91 adults
with PNH from two phase 2 studies (NCT03181633, NCT03472885) and the phase 3
ALPHA study (NCT04469465; 69 patients, 440 samples). Overall, 74.2% were
female, the median age was 38.0 years (16.9-82.0) and the median body weight
77.0 kg (43.4-143.0). By race, 68.3% were White, 17.0% Asian, 4.9% Black or
African American and the remainder other or missing. Renal function by eGFR
was normal in 58.7%, mildly impaired in 35.1%, moderately impaired in 4.4%,
severely impaired in 1.0% and end-stage in 0.7%; 2.0% had moderate hepatic
impairment. 18.4% of participants received the early liquid-filled capsule
(LFC) and the rest the approved tablet; 26.3% were dosed fasted, 69.8% with a
standard meal and 3.9% with a high-fat meal (Chen 2026 Table 1; study list in
Table S1).

The PK-PD (AP activity) dataset is the 69 ALPHA patients with PNH on
ravulizumab or eculizumab, contributing 475 time-matched AP activity and
danicopan concentration pairs. They were 59.4% female, median 57 years old,
median 70.0 kg (44.6-143.0), 39.1% Asian, and all received tablets with a
standard meal (Table 1, last column).

# Food status and formulation coding

The paper has three food states with the standard meal as reference. The model
uses two register columns, `FED` and `FED_HIGHFAT`:

| Food status | `FED` | `FED_HIGHFAT` | Paper indicators |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fasted | 0 | 0 | FAST = 1 |
| Standard meal (reference) | 1 | 0 | none |
| High-fat meal | 1 | 1 | HIFAT = 1 |

`FORM_DANICOPAN_LFC` is 1 for the liquid-filled capsule and 0 for the tablet.
`DOSE` is the dose of each administration in mg (150 or 200 for the approved
regimens), not the daily total. Doses go into the `depot` with `rate = -2`, so
that the zero-order release lasts the model's D1.

```{r helpers}
# One subject's tid dosing records plus a dense observation grid over the
# final 8 h interval. DOSE comes after amt, as the DOSE register entry asks.
make_events <- function(cov, dose_mg, n_doses = 15, tau = 8, dt = 0.25) {
  t_last <- (n_doses - 1) * tau
  dose_rows <- data.frame(
    time = (seq_len(n_doses) - 1) * tau,
    amt = dose_mg, rate = -2, evid = 1, cmt = "depot"
  )
  obs_rows <- data.frame(
    time = t_last + seq(0, tau, by = dt),
    amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central"
  )
  # The model has two endpoints (Cc and alternative_pathway_activity), so
  # observation rows on the central state also carry dvid = 1; every
  # endpoint column is then returned on each observation row.
  obs_rows$dvid <- 1L
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
  ev$DOSE <- dose_mg
  dplyr::cross_join(cov, ev)
}
t_last <- 14 * 8
```

# Typical-value covariate effects (Figure 2)

Figure 2 is a forest plot of steady-state exposure for the 150 mg tid tablet
regimen, relative to a typical male of 75 kg with normal renal function taking
the tablet with a standard meal. The Results text gives the ratios behind it,
and they follow from the model's covariate equations. Here they are recomputed
with the between-subject variability switched off.

```{r forest-sim}
ref_cov <- data.frame(
  WT = 75, SEXF = 0, RENALIMP_SEV = 0, FED = 1, FED_HIGHFAT = 0,
  FORM_DANICOPAN_LFC = 0, REGION_EASTASIA = 0
)
scen <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  ref_cov |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "Reference", dose = 150),
  ref_cov |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "Female", SEXF = 1, dose = 150),
  ref_cov |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "Severe RI", RENALIMP_SEV = 1, dose = 150),
  ref_cov |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "WT 60 kg", WT = 60, dose = 150),
  ref_cov |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "WT 100 kg", WT = 100, dose = 150),
  ref_cov |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "Fasted", FED = 0, dose = 150),
  ref_cov |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "High-fat meal", FED_HIGHFAT = 1, dose = 150),
  ref_cov |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "200 mg tid", dose = 200)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())

ev_tv <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(scen)), function(i) {
  make_events(scen[i, setdiff(names(scen), "dose")], scen$dose[i])
}))

tv <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
sim_tv <- rxode2::rxSolve(tv, events = ev_tv, keep = "scenario") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r forest-nca}
nca_input <- function(sim, group) {
  sim |>
    dplyr::filter(time >= t_last, !is.na(Cc)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(tad = time - t_last) |>
    dplyr::select(id, dplyr::all_of(group), tad, Cc)
}
tv_conc <- nca_input(sim_tv, "scenario")
tv_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(tv_conc, Cc ~ tad | scenario + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 8, cmax = TRUE, ctrough = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))
tv_wide <- as.data.frame(tv_res$result) |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
tv_ref <- tv_wide |> dplyr::filter(scenario == "Reference")
tv_ratio <- tv_wide |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cmax_ratio = cmax / tv_ref$cmax,
    ctrough_ratio = ctrough / tv_ref$ctrough,
    auc_ratio = auclast / tv_ref$auclast
  )
tv_ratio |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, cmax, ctrough, auclast, cmax_ratio, ctrough_ratio, auc_ratio) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(cmax, ctrough, auclast), ~ signif(.x, 4)),
                dplyr::across(dplyr::ends_with("_ratio"), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Scenario = scenario, "Cmax,ss (ng/mL)" = cmax, "Ctrough,ss (ng/mL)" = ctrough,
    "AUC0-8,ss (ng*h/mL)" = auclast, "Cmax ratio" = cmax_ratio,
    "Ctrough ratio" = ctrough_ratio, "AUC ratio" = auc_ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value steady-state exposure (150 mg tid tablet unless stated) and ratio to the reference participant.")
```

The paper's statements for the same contrasts (Results "Impact of Covariates on
Danicopan Exposure" and Discussion):

```{r forest-compare}
published_ratio <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,        ~metric, ~published, ~source,
  "Female",         "AUC",   1.29, "Results: AUC 29% higher",
  "Severe RI",      "AUC",   1.76, "Results and Discussion: 1.76-fold AUC",
  "Severe RI",      "Cmax",  1.54, "Discussion: 1.54-fold Cmax",
  "WT 100 kg",      "AUC",   0.82, "Results: decreased by ~18%",
  "WT 60 kg",       "AUC",   1.16, "Results: increased by up to 16%",
  "Fasted",         "AUC",   0.87, "Results: AUC 0.87-fold",
  "High-fat meal",  "AUC",   1.10, "Results: AUC 1.10-fold",
  "Fasted",         "Cmax",  0.93, "Results: Cmax 0.93-fold",
  "High-fat meal",  "Cmax",  1.55, "Results: Cmax 1.55-fold"
)
sim_ratio <- tv_ratio |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, Cmax = cmax_ratio, AUC = auc_ratio) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-scenario, names_to = "metric", values_to = "simulated")
forest_cmp <- published_ratio |>
  dplyr::left_join(sim_ratio, by = c("scenario", "metric")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated / published - 1))
forest_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(simulated = round(simulated, 3), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Scenario = scenario, Metric = metric, Published = published,
    Simulated = simulated, "% diff" = pct_diff, Source = source
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value exposure ratios vs the ratios stated in Chen 2026.")

# The AUC ratios depend only on F and CL/F, so they must reproduce the stated
# ratios to rounding. The Cmax ratios also depend on absorption and on the
# between-subject variability that Figure 2 includes, so they get a wider band.
auc_rows <- forest_cmp$metric == "AUC"
stopifnot(
  all(abs(forest_cmp$pct_diff[auc_rows]) < 3),
  abs(forest_cmp$pct_diff[forest_cmp$scenario == "Severe RI" & forest_cmp$metric == "Cmax"]) < 10
)
```

The 200 mg vs 150 mg contrast: dose-normalised AUC at 200 mg is
`r round(tv_ratio$auc_ratio[tv_ratio$scenario == "200 mg tid"] * 150 / 200, 3)`
of the 150 mg value, matching the "7% decrease in bioavailability at a dose of
200 mg tid compared with 150 mg tid" ((200/150)^-0.232 = 0.935).

The high-fat Cmax ratio reproduces the paper (1.55-fold). The fasted Cmax
ratio falls between the 0.93-fold quoted in the Results text and Table 3,
whose fasted / standard-meal median Cmax,ss ratios are 487 / 576 = 0.85
(150 mg) and 597 / 726 = 0.82 (200 mg). The model's fasted state combines a
13% lower bioavailability with much faster absorption (ka 32.5 vs 1.58 1/h),
no lag time and a slightly longer zero-order release, and the zero-order step
then limits the peak.

## Absolute exposure of the reference patient (Figure 2)

Figure 2 also gives absolute values: its solid vertical line marks the median
exposure of 1000 simulated reference patients (male, 75 kg, normal renal
function, 150 mg tid tablet with a standard meal) with between-subject
variability. Digitised by the maintainers from the gridlines of each panel,
these are Cmax,ss 389 ng/mL, Ctrough,ss 125 ng/mL and AUC24h,ss 5950 ng*h/mL.
The dashed 80% and 125% lines in each panel sit at 0.80 and 1.25 times those
readings, which confirms the readings. The same scenario is simulated here
with between-subject variability for 200 reference patients.

```{r fig2-abs}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260210)
n_ref <- 200
ref_cohort <- ref_cov[rep(1, n_ref), ] |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = seq_len(n_ref), scenario = "Reference, 150 mg tid")
sim_ref <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events = make_events(ref_cohort, 150), keep = "scenario"
) |>
  as.data.frame()
ref_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_input(sim_ref, "scenario"), Cc ~ tad | scenario + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 8, cmax = TRUE, ctrough = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))
# AUC24h,ss / 3 is compared with the 8 h interval AUC.
published_fig2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,                ~cmax, ~ctrough, ~auclast,
  "Reference, 150 mg tid",  389,   125,      5950 / 3
)
cmp_fig2 <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = ref_res,
  reference = published_fig2,
  by = "scenario",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", ctrough = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp_fig2,
  caption = "Reference patient, simulated (PKNCA median of 200) vs the Figure 2 median read from the plot. AUC0-8 reference = AUC24h,ss / 3."
)
pct_fig2 <- as.numeric(gsub("[*%+]", "", cmp_fig2$`% diff`))
# The covariates match Figure 2 exactly here, so this is the like-for-like
# check of the absolute exposure scale.
stopifnot(!anyNA(pct_fig2), all(abs(pct_fig2) < 15))
```

# Virtual ALPHA cohort and steady-state simulation (Table 3, Figure 3)

Table 3 and Figure 3 simulate 150 mg and 200 mg tid tablets under the three
food states in patients with PNH, sampling covariates (body weight, sex, East
Asian origin) from the ALPHA population and using the ALPHA patients' post-hoc
parameters. The individual post-hoc estimates are not published, so here the
covariates are drawn to match ALPHA's Table 1 summary and between-subject
variability comes from the population variances (Tables 2 and 4). 200 virtual
patients are simulated per regimen and food state, and the same 200 covariate
sets are reused in every arm.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260209)
n_sub <- 200
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  # ALPHA median 70 kg, range 44.6-143 (Table 1).
  WT = pmin(pmax(70 * exp(stats::rnorm(n_sub, 0, 0.2)), 44.6), 143),
  SEXF = stats::rbinom(n_sub, 1, 0.594),
  # 39.1% of ALPHA participants were Asian (Table 1), taken as East Asian.
  REGION_EASTASIA = stats::rbinom(n_sub, 1, 0.391),
  RENALIMP_SEV = 0,
  FORM_DANICOPAN_LFC = 0
)
summary(cohort[, c("WT", "SEXF", "REGION_EASTASIA")])
```

```{r sim-arms}
arms <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  dose = c(150, 200),
  food = c("Fasted", "Standard meal", "High-fat meal")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    FED = ifelse(food == "Fasted", 0, 1),
    FED_HIGHFAT = ifelse(food == "High-fat meal", 1, 0),
    regimen = paste0(dose, " mg tid"),
    arm = paste(regimen, food, sep = ", ")
  )

ev_arms <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  cov_i <- cohort |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      FED = arms$FED[i], FED_HIGHFAT = arms$FED_HIGHFAT[i],
      arm = arms$arm[i], regimen = arms$regimen[i], food = arms$food[i],
      id = id + (i - 1) * n_sub
    )
  make_events(cov_i, arms$dose[i])
}))

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events = ev_arms, keep = c("arm", "regimen", "food")
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

The Table 3 percentiles include between-subject variability but not residual
error, so the comparison below uses the individual predictions `Cc` and
`alternative_pathway_activity`, not the residual-perturbed `sim` column.

## Steady-state exposure (PKNCA)

The simulation runs 15 doses (5 days), well past the time needed to reach
steady state, and analyses the final 8 h dosing interval. Time is shifted so
that the interval opens at 0, Cmax,ss and Ctrough,ss (the concentration at the
end of the interval) come from PKNCA, and AUC24h,ss is three times the
interval AUC.

```{r nca}
conc <- nca_input(sim, c("arm", "regimen", "food"))
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ tad | arm + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 8, cmax = TRUE, ctrough = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))
stopifnot(!anyNA(as.data.frame(nca_res$result)$PPORRES))
```

```{r nca-compare}
# Chen 2026 Table 3, medians. AUC24h,ss is divided by 3 to compare with the
# simulated 8 h interval AUC.
published_nca <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                          ~cmax, ~ctrough, ~auc24,
  "150 mg tid, Fasted",          487,   118,      6901,
  "150 mg tid, Standard meal",   576,   147,      8190,
  "150 mg tid, High-fat meal",   912,   143,      9123,
  "200 mg tid, Fasted",          597,   159,      8824,
  "200 mg tid, Standard meal",   726,   177,      10184,
  "200 mg tid, High-fat meal",   1143,  178,      11300
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(auclast = auc24 / 3) |>
  dplyr::select(-auc24)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published_nca,
  by = "arm",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", ctrough = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated (PKNCA, median of 200 virtual patients per arm) vs Chen 2026 Table 3 median steady-state exposure. AUC0-8 reference = Table 3 AUC24h,ss / 3. * differs from reference by >20%."
)
```

The simulated troughs agree with Table 3, but AUC runs about 10-15% lower and
Cmax about 10-25% lower in every arm. The same model reproduces the Figure 2 reference
patient (above), so the gap comes from the cohort, not from the model. Table 3
was simulated from the ALPHA patients' own post-hoc parameters, and the
published cohort was more exposed than its covariates alone predict. The
Results give a mean CL/F of 63 L/h for the ALPHA patients, while the
covariate-predicted typical CL/F for a 70 kg patient is 76 L/h for a man and
59 L/h for a woman. A shift that applies to every arm leaves the food and dose
contrasts between arms intact, and those agree with the paper (see the ratios
above).

```{r nca-assert}
pct <- as.numeric(gsub("[*%+]", "", cmp$`% diff`))
# Structural check on the centre: a wrong clearance, dose or unit would move
# every arm by tens of percent. The envelope allows for the virtual cohort
# standing in for the ALPHA post-hoc parameters.
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(pct),
  abs(stats::median(pct)) < 20,
  stats::quantile(abs(pct), 0.9) < 35
)
```

Table 3 also reports the share of patients whose Ctrough,ss reaches the IC90
of 108 ng/mL:

```{r ic90}
ic90 <- 108
trough <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "ctrough") |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim_pct_ge_ic90 = 100 * mean(PPORRES >= ic90), .groups = "drop")
published_ic90 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                         ~pub_pct_ge_ic90,
  "150 mg tid, Fasted",         58.2,
  "150 mg tid, Standard meal",  74.5,
  "150 mg tid, High-fat meal",  73.6,
  "200 mg tid, Fasted",         82.9,
  "200 mg tid, Standard meal",  86.1,
  "200 mg tid, High-fat meal",  86.5
)
ic90_cmp <- published_ic90 |>
  dplyr::left_join(trough, by = "arm")
ic90_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(sim_pct_ge_ic90 = round(sim_pct_ge_ic90, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Arm = arm, "Published % with Ctrough,ss >= IC90" = pub_pct_ge_ic90,
    "Simulated %" = sim_pct_ge_ic90
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Share of patients with steady-state trough at or above the IC90 (108 ng/mL), Chen 2026 Table 3.")
stopifnot(abs(stats::median(ic90_cmp$sim_pct_ge_ic90 - ic90_cmp$pub_pct_ge_ic90)) < 15)
```

## AP activity at trough

```{r ap-trough}
ap_trough <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time == t_last + 8) |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    sim_median = stats::median(alternative_pathway_activity),
    sim_p025 = stats::quantile(alternative_pathway_activity, 0.025),
    sim_p975 = stats::quantile(alternative_pathway_activity, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
published_ap <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                         ~pub_median, ~pub_range,
  "150 mg tid, Fasted",         4.9,         "1.8-43.8",
  "150 mg tid, Standard meal",  4.6,         "1.7-42.3",
  "150 mg tid, High-fat meal",  4.5,         "1.8-42.1",
  "200 mg tid, Fasted",         4.4,         "1.7-41.3",
  "200 mg tid, Standard meal",  4.2,         "1.8-39.9",
  "200 mg tid, High-fat meal",  4.2,         "1.7-39.7"
)
ap_cmp <- published_ap |>
  dplyr::left_join(ap_trough, by = "arm")
ap_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    sim = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", sim_median, sim_p025, sim_p975)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(arm, pub_median, pub_range, sim) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Arm = arm, "Published median (%)" = pub_median,
    "Published 2.5th-97.5th" = pub_range, "Simulated median (2.5th-97.5th)" = sim
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "AP activity at steady-state trough (%), Chen 2026 Table 3 vs simulation.")

# Every arm should sit in near-complete inhibition (< 10% activity), as the
# paper concludes, with a median close to the published 4-5%. The tails are
# not compared: the published 97.5th percentiles (about 40%) come from the
# ALPHA patients' post-hoc IC50 and baseline values, and the virtual cohort's
# tails are narrower.
stopifnot(
  all(ap_cmp$sim_median < 10),
  abs(stats::median(ap_cmp$sim_median - ap_cmp$pub_median)) < 1.5
)
```

## Steady-state profiles (Figure 3)

```{r fig3-pk, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
prof <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= t_last) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - t_last) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, food, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cc_med = stats::median(Cc),
    cc_lo = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.025),
    cc_hi = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.975),
    ap_med = stats::median(alternative_pathway_activity),
    ap_lo = stats::quantile(alternative_pathway_activity, 0.025),
    ap_hi = stats::quantile(alternative_pathway_activity, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(food = factor(food, levels = c("Fasted", "Standard meal", "High-fat meal")))

ggplot(prof, aes(tad, cc_med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = cc_lo, ymax = cc_hi), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 108, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_grid(regimen ~ food) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Danicopan (ng/mL)",
    title = "Replicates Figure 3A of Chen 2026",
    caption = "Median and 2.5th-97.5th percentiles of 200 virtual patients per arm; dashed line = IC90 (108 ng/mL)."
  )
```

```{r fig3-ap, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
ggplot(prof, aes(tad, ap_med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ap_lo, ymax = ap_hi), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(regimen ~ food) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "AP activity (%)",
    title = "Replicates Figure 3B of Chen 2026",
    caption = "Median and 2.5th-97.5th percentiles of 200 virtual patients per arm."
  )
```

## Concentration-AP relationship

At the typical baseline (69 kg, not East Asian) the model gives the IC50 and
the IC90 that the paper reports; IC90 = 9 x IC50 for a hyperbolic Emax model.

```{r ec-curve, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
conc_grid <- c(0, 10^seq(-1, 3.5, length.out = 200))
ap_typ <- 29.1 - (29.1 - 3.05) * conc_grid / (12 + conc_grid)
stopifnot(abs(9 * 12 - 108) < 1e-9)
ggplot(data.frame(conc = conc_grid, ap = ap_typ), aes(conc, ap)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(12, 108), linetype = c("dotted", "dashed")) +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log1p", breaks = c(0, 1, 10, 100, 1000)) +
  labs(x = "Danicopan (ng/mL)", y = "AP activity (%)",
       caption = "Typical patient; dotted = IC50 (12 ng/mL), dashed = IC90 (108 ng/mL).")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

1. **The supplement control streams are earlier runs, not the final models.**
   The PK stream carries initial estimates (for example CL 81.4 L/h, Vc 173
   L), holds the high-fat-meal effects on D1 and ka at 0 and has no lag time.
   The PK-PD stream carries a Japan effect on IC50 and factor D and sex effects
   on the baseline that the final model does not retain. Every value in the
   model therefore comes from Tables 2 and 4 and the printed equations. The
   streams settle the structure: ADVAN4, the combined residual error, the
   `S2 = V2/1000` units, the additive random effect on the AP baseline and the
   proportional AP residual error.
2. **High-fat meal on ka is exponential.** The printed Ka equation multiplies
   by e^(1.09 if HIFAT), giving a 2.97-fold ka with a high-fat meal. The
   earlier control stream uses `(1 + THETA(24))`, which would give 2.09-fold.
   The equation is followed.
3. **The fasted effect on ka is additive.** Following the Ka equation and the
   control stream (`+ THETA(23) * FAST`), fasting adds 30.9 1/h to the tablet
   ka (32.5 1/h in total). Once the zero-order release has finished, absorption
   is then almost immediate.
4. **Lag time.** The Tlag equation defines a lag only for tablets taken with a
   standard meal (0.278 h) or a high-fat meal (0.293 h). Fasted tablet doses
   and LFC doses get no lag time.
5. **Residual-error units.** Table 2 labels the proportional PK error as "%"
   with the value 0.435. The control stream's initial value for the same
   theta is 0.445 on the fractional scale, so the estimate is read as 0.435
   (43.5%). Table 4's 67.1% is read as 0.671.
6. **IIV on IC50.** Table 4 reports omega^2 = 5.26 for IC50 with "229%". That
   percentage is 100 x sqrt(omega^2) rather than the 100 x sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)
   used in Table 2; the variance 5.26 is used as printed.
7. **AP baseline random effect is additive** (SD 9.5 percentage points), so a
   low-weight East Asian virtual patient can occasionally get a baseline near
   or below 0. The observed baselines in ALPHA ranged from 0.56% to 109%.
8. **PK-PD driver.** The source fitted AP against observed, time-matched
   danicopan concentrations. The packaged model drives AP with the
   model-predicted `Cc`, which is how the authors' own simulations use it.
9. **Severe renal impairment indicator.** Table 1 lists 4 participants with
   severe impairment and 3 with end-stage disease, while the Discussion refers
   to eight participants with severe renal impairment. The paper does not say
   how the end-stage participants were coded. Set `RENALIMP_SEV = 1` for eGFR
   < 30 mL/min/1.73 m^2.
10. **East Asian origin.** The paper's covariate is participation from East
    Asia. Table 1 gives only the share of Asian participants (39.1% in
    ALPHA), which the virtual cohort uses as the East Asian share.
11. **Virtual cohort instead of post-hoc parameters.** Table 3 and Figure 3
    use the ALPHA patients' post-hoc parameters, which are not published. The
    simulation here draws covariates from the Table 1 summary and random
    effects from the population variances. That explains the remaining gaps
    against Table 3, and is why the comparison checks medians and robust
    quantiles rather than individual extremes.
